stimulus.title: A side chain in the core of an enzyme
stimulus.text: An enzyme that works dissolved in the watery fluid inside cells folds into a compact shape. Position 88 of its polypeptide is valine, whose side chain is nonpolar, and in the folded enzyme this side chain is buried in the center of the molecule. Researchers compare the normal enzyme with two versions made from altered genes: in one, valine 88 is replaced by glutamic acid (a negatively charged side chain); in the other, by isoleucine (a nonpolar side chain slightly larger than valine's).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Describe where nonpolar side chains are usually found in a folded protein that works in water, and why.

rubric.point: States that nonpolar side chains are usually buried in the interior (core), because they are hydrophobic and water molecules hydrogen-bond with each other and push them together (hydrophobic interactions).
accept: inside the protein, away from water, because they are hydrophobic
clustered in the core by hydrophobic interactions

parts.sample: Nonpolar side chains are usually buried in the core of the folded protein. They are hydrophobic: water molecules hydrogen-bond with each other and with polar side chains on the surface, so the nonpolar side chains are pushed together inside, away from water (hydrophobic interactions).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain how replacing valine 88 with glutamic acid would affect the enzyme's tertiary structure.

rubric.point: Explains that a charged side chain cannot take part in the hydrophobic interactions of the core and is unstable buried away from water, so the chain would fold differently (or partly unfold), changing the tertiary structure.
accept: the negative charge disrupts the hydrophobic core, so the 3-D shape changes
the polypeptide would refold to move the charged side chain toward water, changing its shape

parts.sample: Glutamic acid's side chain carries a negative charge, so it is hydrophilic and does not fit among the nonpolar side chains of the core. It disrupts the hydrophobic interactions that hold the core together, so the chain folds into a different shape or partly unfolds: its tertiary structure changes.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Predict the effect of the glutamic acid replacement on the enzyme's function, and justify your prediction.

rubric.point: Predicts reduced or lost activity, justified by the change in shape: the enzyme's function depends on its specific 3-D shape.
accept: activity drops because the enzyme no longer has the shape it needs
it would work poorly or not at all, since structure determines function

parts.sample: The enzyme would lose most or all of its activity. An enzyme works because of its precise 3-D shape, and the misfolded version no longer has that shape.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Explain why replacing valine 88 with isoleucine is likely to have little effect on the enzyme's function.

rubric.point: Explains that isoleucine is also nonpolar, so it still fits the hydrophobic core and takes part in the same hydrophobic interactions; the shape, and so the function, changes little.
accept: isoleucine is nonpolar like valine, so the core stays hydrophobic and the fold is kept
similar side chain chemistry keeps the same tertiary structure

parts.sample: Isoleucine's side chain is nonpolar like valine's, so it still packs into the hydrophobic core and joins the same hydrophobic interactions. The folded shape barely changes, so the enzyme keeps nearly all of its function.
